findings.trigger: Use an IActor with a supported category alias such as categoryId:planet (accepted by validator and explicitly regression-tested in validateDatabase.spec.ts).
findings.impact: Actor.category returns null because belongsTo compares the string alias with Category.id. UI ObjectList dereferences category with non-null assertions; category-specific runtime/body-info behavior loses category identity.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe new Actor({id:999,categoryId:planet}).category returns null while categories includes alias planet. IActor permits numeric or alias categoryId; validator accepts this. Category.actors similarly only uses numeric IDs; GenericForm nebula routing/hasInvalidInput only resolve numeric category IDs. Cross-module caller trace: RenderableFactory.make:93 switches only numeric IDs 1..12 and throws on an alias; DynamicNode.isOriented:58-62 explicitly excludes string IDs; atmosphere/ring material queries use numeric IDs. Fixing only Actor.category would not make aliases functional.
findings.decisionNeeded: Choose whether category aliases remain supported throughout runtime/editor relations or are normalized to numeric IDs at a single boundary; apply consistently to Actor.category, reverse relations and category-dependent editor logic.

findings.trigger: Open Ceres body info in the Solar system.
findings.impact: Ceres mass, density, surface gravity and escape velocity are based on a sub-nanogram mass for a 469.7 km-radius body, so the displayed physical quantities are invalid.
findings.evidence: Shipped Ceres physical row id6/actorId9 stores mass5.21e-10 (mass contract is kg) and radius469.7 (km). Source-derived density is 1.2002934425010829e-30 g/cm3. Other Solar-system masses use kg values such as 3.3022e23 for Mercury. No replacement scientific value guessed.
findings.decisionNeeded: Owner should confirm intended Ceres mass/source and units; review historical physical table values before regenerating the data.

findings.trigger: Call the public Storage.disk(s3) selector and use its declared Storage return.
findings.impact: Selector returns the string s3, not a Storage object/facade; it also changes a process-wide static driver. No current callers found, so no present application-path failure claimed.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe logs Storage.disk(s3) === string s3. Implementation returns the assignment this.driver=driver, while the signature promises Storage. Empty instance shape lets TypeScript miss the mismatch.
findings.decisionNeeded: Decide whether to retain a global void selector, provide an actual per-disk facade, or remove this unused API; current return contract is demonstrably false.

findings.validation: GPU regression: before fix, center impulse centroid (15.875,15.875) and symmetry errors 4/4/4/8; after correcting center UV and four border masks, Chromium SwiftShader probe passes.

findings.impact: midbandSlopeBound is not a global Lipschitz bound for actual height. CameraCollision uses it to choose march steps (lines522 and598), so its no-tunneling reasoning does not hold for supported settings. A visible tunnel has not been reproduced.
findings.evidence: Production TerrainHeightField, zonal slope0.3, radius1000km, map2048x1024 [-40000,40000], waterLevelMeters0, midbandWaterFadeMeters1 (all accepted settings): published bound2.8035, midbandTilt21.1868324, actual height-band central derivative19.3494819 at latitude arc1.1011011m. Scratch terrain-probe.ts. sample includes strength*height*envGrad at lines266-267 but constructor bound covers only noise/warp with frozen direction. Existing bound tests use fixed/wide envelope.
findings.trigger: A valid narrow midbandWaterFadeMeters creates rapidly varying coast envelope. Same issue can arise from terrain-dependent envelope/flow derivatives absent from the bound.
findings.decisionNeeded: Choose a conservative bound including envelope and flow-direction variation, restrict supported fade/parameter ranges with an explicit contract, or adopt collision marching that remains safe without a global derivative bound. Account for runtime cost before changing marching.

findings.trigger: AsteroidBelt hides its streamer on transition from Near to Mid/Far; SceneManager traverses all objects.
findings.impact: Streamer does not immediately deactivate sectors and continues invisible cascade work; breaks intended sleep lifecycle.
findings.evidence: AsteroidBelt sets streamer.visible; isEffectivelyVisible starts at parent. SceneManager.ts:114 calls scene.traverse. Scratch hidden-system frame observes zero deactivateAll calls.
findings.smallFix: Check this.visible before traversing parents; no-this-alias lint remains satisfied.
findings.regression: AsteroidBeltNode.spec.ts: actual belt.traverse after 20 Near frames, transition to Mid/Far (height .2/2 AU) immediately empties pool and sectors, return Near reuses streamer and repopulates. Both cases failed red with 316 residual active sectors.

findings.trigger: Optional editable dustScaleHeightFraction is zero, negative or nonfinite; zero passes database field validation.
findings.impact: Zero height makes calibrated dust density Infinity (NaN when tau is also zero), entering GPU uniforms and invalidating dust calculations.
findings.evidence: Scratch test creates actual AsteroidBelt with fraction=0 and confirms Number.isFinite(uDustDensity) is false; validator has no optional-height check.
findings.smallFix: Positive finite fraction or default 1/3; preserve valid positive values.
findings.regression: AsteroidBeltParameters tests zero, negative, NaN, +/-Infinity fallback and valid positive preservation. AsteroidBeltNode constructs actual dust volume with zero height and tau0/.06; finite density and positive height verified.

findings.evidence: Red FakePlanet regression moved camera.x20->5 for body.x10:color/base remained0.05 instead1. Phase/color moved intact to updateView;new regression plus math/eclipse/camera tests pass.

findings.trigger: Regression test claims the actual raster proxy fits the far plane for arbitrary orientation and 1.3x camera retreat.
findings.impact: The passing test proves a bound for the former [-1,1] proxy; current NebulaVolume uses BoxGeometry(4,4,4), so this claimed geometric guarantee is false. No runtime rendering failure is claimed.
findings.evidence: Crab shell size 900 AU; camera distance hypot(1280,1280)=1810.193 AU. Test: distance*1.3 + size*sqrt(3)=3912.097 AU < 5000. Actual proxy bound: distance*1.3 + 2*size*sqrt(3)=5470.943 AU > 5000. NebulaVolume.ts:41 constructs BoxGeometry(4,4,4). docs/crab-remnant-handoff.md section 3 repeats former bound. Current extreme near/far projection rounds the float32 z coefficient to -1; therefore this is a stale test/document guarantee, not evidence that current Crab pixels clip.
findings.disposition: Deferred: review geometric guard/documentation independently; do not change camera, far plane or assertion tolerance during this audit.
